topic: witness testifies in crimes against humanity case
headline_marked: Witness: [[Protester dragged out and shot dead]] in Mohammadpur during July Uprising
headline: Witness: Protester dragged out and shot dead in Mohammadpur during July Uprising
summary: A prosecution witness told the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that a man seeking shelter from gunfire was forcibly removed from a building and killed at close range.
details: A prosecution witness testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 today regarding the events of the July Uprising in Dhaka's Mohammadpur area.
The witness, Md Mamun Farazi, stated that he saw a protester named Raju being dragged out of a residential building where he was seeking shelter from gunfire.
According to the testimony, a police officer and an Ansar member shot Raju at close range in the leg and abdomen, leading to his death later that day.
Farazi testified that the events took place on July 19, 2024, around 2:30 pm near the Allah Karim Mosque in Mohammadpur.
He described a scene of repeated firing by police, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), Ansar, and armed men affiliated with the Awami League and its student and youth wings.
The witness also recounted seeing another protester, identified as Jasim, collapse after being shot in the chest and fingers.
Farazi helped take Jasim to a pharmacy and then to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital, but Jasim died on July 29.
These testimonies are part of a crimes against humanity case against former DSCC mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former minister Jahangir Kabir Nanak, and 26 others.
caption:
A protester seeking shelter was dragged out of a building and shot at close range, a witness told the ICT.

A prosecution witness testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 today regarding the events of the July Uprising in Dhaka's Mohammadpur area.

The witness, Md Mamun Farazi, stated that he saw a protester named Raju being dragged out of a residential building where he was seeking shelter from gunfire.

According to the testimony, a police officer and an Ansar member shot Raju at close range in the leg and abdomen, leading to his death later that day.

Farazi testified that the events took place on July 19, 2024, around 2:30 pm near the Allah Karim Mosque in Mohammadpur.

He described a scene of repeated firing by police, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), Ansar, and armed men affiliated with the Awami League and its student and youth wings.

The witness also recounted seeing another protester, identified as Jasim, collapse after being shot in the chest and fingers.

Farazi helped take Jasim to a pharmacy and then to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital, but Jasim died on July 29.

These testimonies are part of a crimes against humanity case against former DSCC mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former minister Jahangir Kabir Nanak, and 26 others.

topic: Jinnah images displayed at Ducsu museum spark controversy
headline_marked: DU student [[tears up Jinnah images]] at Ducsu archive
headline: DU student tears up Jinnah images at Ducsu archive
summary: A student protested the display of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah's photos at the Ducsu museum, while a photo of Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes is now on display.
details: A Dhaka University student tore up three photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan, at the Ducsu archive museum.
The act was a protest against the display of Jinnah's images in the university's collection.
Simultaneously, the museum has added a photograph showing Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes.
The Ducsu archive serves as a collection of historical documents and photos related to student politics and the history of Bangladesh.
This development comes amid a broader trend of reviewing and updating historical displays in public institutions across the country.
